title: Per-peer link keys
close_reason: Closed as superseded by the unified identity/trust model; no code changes required. Normative evidence: spec/06-security.md §§8.5/8.7 says all identity derives from one Ed25519 keypair, "One key for all purposes," no pre-shared network keys, and per-peer trust is TOFU pinning of the complete public key to IID/native address. spec/drafts/draft-lichen-link-01.md §4.1 says the link signing key is the sender long-term Ed25519 private key and the corresponding public key is announced or pre-provisioned; §4.3 performs per-peer candidate lookup and signature verification. Thus "per-peer link keys" means pinned peer public-key/trust/replay state, not a separately derived symmetric key. Python LinkLayer implements bounded per-IID TOFU pins, key-change rejection, per-public-key replay/generation state, rotation, and persistence; Rust lichen-link LinkLayer/trust implements the same. Verification: Python test_link_rx + test_link_security_persistence 57 passed; Rust link_layer filter 35 passed and trust filter 2 passed. No C/Zephyr prerequisite is needed to resolve this stale design bead because introducing per-peer symmetric keys would contradict the current spec.
